prompt:
Reports from three customer-facing teams, all about things turning up where they should not.

1. Support: a customer found a label on one of their issues that carries another customer's project name; nobody in their workspace created it. The label picker had been sent a stale set of label ids.
2. Support: an issue was created as a sub-issue of an issue that belongs to a different workspace, another one under an issue from a different project of the same workspace, and a third under an issue that had been archived. None of these parents can be seen from where the sub-issues live.
3. Support: a reply "vanished": it had been posted as a reply to a comment on a different issue, and another one as a reply to a comment that had already been deleted, so neither shows in any thread.
4. Security: an issue was assigned to a person who is not a member of the workspace (they received the assignment email), a project was created with a stranger as its lead, and someone who had left the workspace was @-mentioned through the composer's suggestions and got notified.

Expected behaviour. Everything a change points at must be usable from the workspace the change is made in. An assignee or a project lead must be a current member of that workspace. Labels must be that workspace's own labels, and an issue never shows a label that is not, whatever was attached to it before. A parent issue must be a live issue of the same project. A reply must be to a live, top-level comment on the same issue. People mentioned in a comment, whether written as @handles or supplied by the composer, are only ever current members of the workspace: mentions of anyone else are ignored, not refused, and never notified. A reference to something that belongs to another workspace is refused the same way as any other cross-workspace access. A reference that does not exist, is archived or deleted, is not a current member, is a parent from a different project, or is a reply to a reply is refused as not found. A refused change changes nothing: no issue or comment is created, no field or label is changed, and nothing is announced.

This is a `fix` task: edit the code and stop. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
notes: Root cause (contract between the schema, service and repository layers): a write may reference other rows (assignee, project lead, labels, parent issue, parent comment, mentions) and nothing owns referential integrity across tenants. Zod validates only the id shape; repositories filter reads by org_id, so a service never learns whether a referenced id is a row in another workspace, a missing row, an archived row or a non-member; and the issue->labels join joins on label id alone, so a foreign label attached through any path decorates the issue. Injected (bug.patch, 1 file): comment-service stopped filtering the composer-supplied mention ids against the member list (comment: the composer resolves them from the same list), so a stranger or a former member can be mentioned and notified. Everything else the prompt describes is latent in the pristine corpus: labels from another org accepted on create/update, parent issues from another org / project / archived accepted, replies to comments on other issues, deleted comments or replies accepted (and never rendered, because the thread is one level deep), assignees and leads who are not members accepted (the assignment notification then goes to a non-member). Reference fix (10 files, 3 layers, ~222 changed lines): lib/tenant assertReferenceInOrg; services/_support requireReference / requireLiveReference (missing -> NotFoundError, foreign -> TenantScopeError checked first, archived -> NotFoundError); label-repository findLabelsByIds (deliberately unscoped reference lookup) and an org-safe issue->labels join; issue-repository findIssueForReference and comment-repository findCommentForReference (unscoped reference lookups); member-repository isActiveMember; member-service assertActiveMember; issue-service validates assignee, parent (live, same project) and the whole label set before any write in create/update/assign; project-service validates the lead on create/update; comment-service validates a reply's parent (live, same issue, top-level) and filters mentions to active members again. Traps: the codebase's rule that every repository read is org-scoped makes the natural lookup return "missing" for a foreign row, but the prompt requires a foreign reference to be refused as a cross-workspace access (TenantScopeError), so the reference lookups must be by id alone and the scope check applied to the row; validating after the repository write leaves partial label writes; the read-side join must also be org-safe for previously attached foreign labels; a reply to a reply looks harmless in a tree model but the thread renders one level, so it must be refused. Validation: bug -> git apply clean, tsc 0, visible 617/617 (no visible edits needed); hidden 16/19 fail; bug+solution -> hidden 19/19, full 636/636, tsc 0; naive A (revert the injected mention filter only) 15/19 fail; naive B (full validation but every bad reference reported as not_found through org-scoped lookups, join untouched) 5/19 fail (the five cross-workspace cases: not_found instead of TenantScopeError, and the planted foreign label still shown); naive C (full solution except a reply to a reply is accepted) 1/19 fail (reply to a reply accepted); hidden x3 stable.
